body:
### Neovim version (nvim -v) 0.9.0-dev 0ef6aaa3a73d5089bf53e804364950c81784574c ### Vim (not Nvim) behaves the same? n/a ### Operating system/version Ubuntu 18.04 WSL ### Terminal name/version Kitty N/A ### $TERM environment variable xterm-256color N/A ### Installation Manually compiled ### How to reproduce the issue The issue seems to be memory corruption that can occur if I execute [my `:Rg ` ripgrep integration](https://github.com/mqudsi/vim-ripgrep/blob/master/plugin/vim-ripgrep.vim) by executing `:Rg -F tmpname(` while cd'd into the neovim codebase. I think it might have to do with the speed that the results are returned at, since it seems to replicate with what is functionally `ripgrep -F ...` more often than with `ripgrep ...` It doesn't happen every time (and seems to take longer to reproduce if gdb is attached) but reproduces rather readily when I'm editing the neovim codebase and ripgrepping the same. Note that in the stack trace you can observe the invalid `old_last` being passed in to `qf_update_buffer()` from `qf_init_ext()`. ### Expected behavior No segfault. ### Actual behavior Segfault due to bad memory access.
